Watts made this hymn from Psalm 120, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1In my distress I cried to the LORD, and He answered me. 2Deliver my soul, O LORD, from lying lips and a deceitful tongue. 3What will He do to you, and what will be added to you, O deceitful tongue? 4Sharp arrows will come from the warrior, with burning coals of the broom tree! … 3 more verses PSALM 120 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 120
Peace is the blessing that I seek, How lovely are its charms; I am for peace; but when I speak, They all declare for arms. STANZA IV
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 120. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
